questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Scaling the centripetal force with speed
questions.learningObjective: Identify how centripetal force scales with speed
questions.stem: A marine biologist notes a fish swimming in a circle; if speed doubles at fixed radius, how does centripetal force change?

options.text: It quadruples, since force scales with speed squared
It doubles, since force scales linearly with speed
options.misconception: assumes linear rather than squared scaling

options.text: It halves, since faster motion reduces curvature
It stays the same, since radius is unchanged
options.misconception: ignores speed in the force formula

questions.explanation: Centripetal force F = m v^2/r, so doubling speed quadruples force at fixed radius and mass. Radius alone does not set force.
questions.hint: Force scales with speed squared.

questions.topic: What caps the cornering speed

options.text: The vehicle's mass alone
options.misconception: treats mass as the limiting factor

options.text: The maximum static friction between tires and road
The curve's radius alone
The vehicle's engine power

questions.explanation: On a flat curve, friction provides centripetal force; when required force exceeds maximum static friction, the vehicle skids. Mass and radius affect the required force.
questions.hint: Friction limits the centripetal force.

questions.topic: Relative velocity of two crossing vehicles
questions.learningObjective: Compute relative speed for new values
questions.stem: Two boats cross at 8 m/s north and 15 m/s east; what is their relative speed in m/s?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = sqrt(8^2+15^2) = 17 m/s. Perpendicular velocities combine by Pythagoras.
questions.hint: Use Pythagoras for perpendicular velocities.
